title: The Daily Purification of the Soul from the Archonic Mingling
arc: From the recognition that the whole archonic host of darkness lies within the soul, the teaching moves to how the soul, by receiving nourishment day by day, habitually purifies, cleanses, and filters out the Darkness mingled into her.
reading:
This short teaching describes how Divine Light, having entered the soul, performs its redemptive work upon the darkness still mingled within her. It opens with the sober recognition that what the soul must "grasp" — that is, take hold of consciously — is "the entire archonic host that exists within him." The cosmic battle is not external but interior: the whole company of ruling falsities-from-evil, the proprium in its many subordinate forms, has its lodging inside the human soul itself. This is the precondition of regeneration: the soul must see that the Land of Darkness she is to overcome lies within her own natural mind.

The teaching then turns, in its second point, to how the Light actually proceeds against this internal host. It is not by some single dramatic stroke but by a continuous, daily operation. The soul "comes in" — that is, comes inward to her interior life — through what the surviving text calls a dispensation of nourishment "day by day." This nourishment is the influx of Divine Truth received in regular, ordered measure: the soul fed continually by the Living Spirit's daily food, the truths and goods that come down as her sustenance. Because the food is divine, it carries a sorting power within it; the very act of eating is the act of cleansing.

The arc reaches its center in the chain of verbs: she purifies, she cleanses, she filters, she washes forth the mingling. These are not four different acts but one regenerative work seen at four registers — the same process by which the heavenly drops enter the salt sea and slowly draw out from it the pearl. What is being washed forth is precisely the "mingling," the conjoined state of truth and falsity that constitutes the soul's present condition. And the teaching closes by naming what is being separated out: "the Darkness which is mingled into her." The Darkness here is the falsity-from-evil that has interpenetrated the soul's substance — the residue and presence of the archonic host named at the opening.

So the whole argument is a tight movement: (1) the host of darkness is within; (2) the soul receives Light's nourishment daily; (3) that daily nourishment is itself the filtering action; (4) what it filters out is the mingled Darkness. The teaching is therefore about regeneration as a steady, dietary, daily work of separation — not a momentary deliverance but the patient operation by which Divine Truth, taken in as bread, sorts the soul from within. The lacunae do not disturb this arc; the surviving verbs (purify, cleanse, filter, wash forth) are decisive and converge on a single doctrine: the Light that has come into the soul works through ordinary daily reception to expel, particle by particle, the darkness it finds mingled there.
